messages:
julia (Customer): Hey team — over the last 10 minutes our service started getting intermittent 429s from Redwood. We send all traffic through our proxy which reuses a pool of NAT IPs, and each request includes our API key in Authorization. Billing shows a sudden token spike too. Any ideas?

sara (Support): Sorry about that, julia. Can you paste a sample curl and a request-id from one of the 429 responses? Also which API key (masked) and the nat IP range if possible.

julia (Customer): Sample curl below — the 429 response header had x-request-id: req_01HxyzT and x-rate-limit: 100/60. Our proxy IP observed was 35.182.12.45. API key mask: rk-***9a3.

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer rk-XXXX9a3" \n  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.2.14, 54.210.3.8" \n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```

julia (Customer): Also sometimes requests are signed by our org-token for internal tooling (org: org-77) — we recently rotated keys. Not sure if that matters.

ratebot: Deployment notice: routing-rule v3.4 deployed to infra in us-east-1 at 2024-11-02T15:45:12Z.

mike (SRE): Thanks — on first pass this looks like an attribution/priority edge. Typically Redwood attributes quota by the strongest auth presented: API key (token) takes precedence, then delegated org identity, and finally client IP if no token. But proxies that rewrite headers or have multiple auth tokens in-flight can create mixed attribution. Two quick checks: are you occasionally sending an org token instead of the API key? And is the proxy stripping the original Authorization header?

julia (Customer): We sometimes issue org-token for internal jobs. Proxy should pass Authorization through untouched but it mutates X-Forwarded-For for true client IP.

sara (Support): Mike, can you check router logs for req_01HxyzT and adjacent req ids from that NAT IP window? If attribution flipped to org-level quota we could have hit a lower org cap.

mike (SRE): Pulling logs.

-- few seconds --

mike (SRE): Found req_01HxyzT and a cluster of requests from 35.182.12.45 at 15:12:03-15:12:18 UTC. Attribution shows mixed identities: some requests authenticated as rk-XXXX9a3, others as org-77 (org token). The quota applied was the org-level burst window (org 77 had a low short-term cap). When the org cap was exceeded router returned 429 with x-rate-scope: org.

sam (Platform): That explains the billing spike too — org attribution aggregated some requests. The proxy's job queue replayed a subset of requests using the org token for retries (internal behavior), so traffic that started under the API key got re-attributed on retry.

julia (Customer): Ah, retries — we do transparent retries for 5xx and occasionally re-sign with a short-lived org token. We thought key-level requests and org-level retries would be merged.

sara (Support): Quick mitigation options: 1) Stop retry path from swapping into org-token so requests keep API-key attribution. 2) Ask us to raise org short-term burst cap while you fix client behavior. 3) Configure per-key quota (if you prefer stricter isolation). Which would you like?

julia (Customer): Can you raise org burst for now and we'll patch our retry logic asap. Also would like guidance to reproduce locally so we can validate.

mike (SRE): Done — I raised org-77 short-term burst cap by +3x for 1 hour (monitoring enabled). To reproduce locally: emulate mixed auth and NAT by making two parallel requests from a single client token and then re-sending a retry with an org token. Example sequence:

```
# 1) normal request with API key
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer rk-XXXX9a3" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'

# 2) simulated retry that uses org token (what your proxy did)
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer org-77-xxxx" -H "X-Forwarded-For: 35.182.12.45" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}'
```

mike (SRE): If you can produce a tight loop that flips auth on retry you'll see org-level counts tick up and then 429 with x-rate-scope: org when the org burst window trips.

sam (Platform): Longer-term recommendations: - prefer single-auth-path: keep retries signed by the original API key. - use per-key project scoping: pin API keys to explicit project quotas so retries won't collide with org fugitive traffic. - if using NATs, enable explicit IP affinity mapping in Console so we can attribute to known customer pools.

julia (Customer): Thanks — we'll push retry change in next 30m and validate with your reproduce steps. Please leave the org bump for 1 hour.

sara (Support): Confirmed: org cap raised until 1735554900. If you still see 429s after the fix, paste new request-ids and we'll dig deeper. :thumbsup: 

julia (Customer): Got it, will report back. Thanks everyone!

mike (SRE): Follow-up note for internal thread: consider adding router-side heuristic to prefer original key attribution when X-Original-Auth or X-Forwarded-Auth headers are present (helpful for proxies rewrites). Filing infra ticket.
